ghrelin.definition: A hormone made mainly in the stomach. It makes you feel hungry and makes the pituitary gland release growth hormone.

ghrelin-receptor.definition: The receptor that ghrelin switches on. It sits on cells in the pituitary gland, the brain, the stomach and other organs. Ipamorelin switches on the same receptor.

pentapeptide.definition: A peptide made of five amino acids joined in a chain.

naphthylalanine.definition: An amino acid that the body does not use to build proteins. It is added in the lab. Ipamorelin contains its mirror-image (D) form.

somatotroph.definition: A cell in the front part of the pituitary gland that makes and releases growth hormone.

pulsatile-secretion.definition: Release of a hormone in short bursts instead of a steady flow. Growth hormone is released in pulses, many of them at night.

acth.definition: A hormone from the pituitary gland that tells the adrenal glands to make cortisol.

cortisol.definition: A stress hormone made by the adrenal glands. Too much for a long time can raise blood sugar and blood pressure.

prolactin.definition: A hormone from the pituitary gland. It starts milk production after birth. Too much can affect periods, fertility and sex drive.

growth-hormone-deficiency.definition: A condition in which the pituitary gland makes too little growth hormone. In children it slows growth. It is diagnosed with special blood tests and treated with approved growth hormone.

postoperative-ileus.definition: A short pause in the movement of the bowel after an operation. Food and gas cannot pass normally, which causes bloating, sickness and a longer hospital stay.

hyperglycaemia.definition: Blood sugar that is higher than normal. Signs include strong thirst, passing a lot of urine and tiredness.

hypokalaemia.definition: Too little potassium in the blood. It can cause muscle weakness, cramps and an irregular heartbeat.

oedema.definition: Swelling caused by fluid building up in the body, often in the ankles, feet or legs.

qt-prolongation.definition: A change in the heart's electrical rhythm, seen on a heart tracing (ECG). It can lead to a dangerous irregular heartbeat.

pharmacodynamics.definition: What a drug does to the body, and how that effect changes with the amount in the blood.

ibutamoren.definition: A swallowed, non-peptide drug that switches on the ghrelin receptor. It was tested in trials but is not an approved medicine.

macimorelin.definition: A medicine taken once by mouth as a test for growth hormone deficiency in adults. It switches on receptors in the pituitary gland. It is approved in the EU and the US.

anamorelin.definition: A tablet that switches on the ghrelin receptor, developed for weight loss in people with lung cancer. The EU refused to approve it in 2017.

serious-adverse-event.definition: A harmful event during a study that leads to death, danger to life, a hospital stay or lasting harm. It is counted whether or not the study drug caused it.

anastomotic-leak.definition: A leak where two ends of the bowel were sewn or stapled back together during an operation. It is a serious complication of bowel surgery.

pharmacopoeia-monograph.definition: An official quality standard for a medicine ingredient: how to test it and what limits it must meet.
